name: sore-throat-name-only
description: Probe (a): receptionist gives own name and practice and asks the caller's name, but never checks who the call is for. Everything else well done.

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Hello, is that the surgery? I need an appointment with the doctor please.

transcript.speaker: trainee
transcript.text: Good morning, Pen-y-Bryn Surgery, Sam speaking. Can I take your name please?

transcript.speaker: trainee
transcript.text: Thank you, Carys. What's the problem?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: I've had a sore throat for two days and I'd like some antibiotics.

transcript.speaker: trainee
transcript.text: Can you swallow drinks and food all right?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Yes, it's sore but I can swallow fine.

transcript.speaker: trainee
transcript.text: Any other health conditions, or regular medicines?

transcript.speaker: trainee
transcript.text: Thank you. The best place is the pharmacy. The pharmacist can check your throat and treat you today if you need it. If you get worse, ring us back.

expect.flagsReason: Pharmacy with a call-back instruction matches the key.

greeting.reason: The guide asks for the name AND checking who is calling and for whom. Own name, practice and the caller's name were done; whether the call was for herself was never checked, so half is missing. A 2 would ignore the "for whom" half of the guide.

explanation.reason: Where, why, and ring back if worse.
